kocaPortraitTrial.prompt: Edit the FIRST attached square raster pixel art UV texture atlas in place. It is a technical unfolded face texture, not a picture of a head facing the viewer. Keep exactly the same square canvas, pixel scale, landmarks and island positions as first image. The second reference is a black and white wartime photo of a man (Koča Popović); use this photo ONLY as a close likeness reference for the face and hair. Do not render his clothing, hat, body, trees, or photographic lighting. Make the man in the central face area of the first atlas look recognizably like the man in the second photo. Particularly reproduce the much narrower and smaller moustache which is thickest at the center under the nose but tapers naturally, ends within the mouth corners and has no drooping ends. Make eyebrows slimmer, softly arched and not angry. The photograph shows deep-set eyes, lean oval cheeks, thin closed lips, a long comparatively narrow straight nose with a rounded tip and dark smooth short hair. Render those traits by deliberate pixel clusters while preserving the underlying 3D landmarks and exact old UV locations of the eyelids, nostrils, lips and ears. Tidy the old deep V at the hairline into a plausible shallow hairline with subtle side part and reduce the thick wavy highlights in the upper hair islands. Preserve the familiar muted warm palette of the first texture, with no hard photorealistic baked shadows from the photograph. Pixel art hard edges, intentional blocky clusters about the same width as old atlas. Outside the upper head and hair islands copy the old original artwork unchanged: the bottom half (hands, mouth-interior, teeth, big separate eyeball), edges, and isolated ears all remain exactly as they were. Same framing and registration. No turning or shifting any part of the UV. No framing, no borders, no new islands, no words, no central bust.
kocaPortraitTrial.registration: Blend the central face into the base cheek and jaw. Keep the base temples and ear UVs. Remove the iris painted into the lids on the skin map and center the separate iris texture using both modeled eye apertures.

prompt: Create 1 new game texture sheet to dress an existing custom 3D character. This is a precise texture-atlas redraw, flat orthographic albedo only, no 3D preview, no typography. Output landscape with two equally sized square panels, edge-to-edge and zero margins or dividing line. LEFT 50% is a position-locked redraw of first reference, the uniform UV atlas. RIGHT 50% is a position-locked redraw of second reference, the head/hands UV atlas. The third reference is style and color only, a small WWII Yugoslav partisan in our own game: use its warm khaki wool jacket and side cap, dark olive trousers (#4c4c34), warm brown leather, peach skin, dark chestnut hair, little red five-pointed star on the cap. Keep each panel's square UV layout EXACT, matching each input island outline, shape, scale, seam, intersection, landmark and material position including front/back figures, the neck on the top of the uniform, belt/button line, at the bottom three large trouser and sleeve islands, boots and two peach hands on right edge, cap patch at normalized x=.457 y=.244. Remove the photographic woodland camouflage from the jacket and replace with plainly colored khaki wool with deliberate pixel clusters depicting collar and pocket seams and blocky folds. The mapped pants are dark muted olive; white/silver buckle and deep brown leather boots. The right face is the same young adult with brown hair in angular clusters, soft natural proportions, keep iris center, mouth, nose, ears, fingers and scalp islands registered exactly so it wraps original. Draw flat hard-edged square pixels with roughly 128px pixel grid per square sheet panel, directed shadow shapes, only 4 shades per material, no texture noise/soft blur/dithering/gloss, no smoothing between color patches. Preserve readable adult features. Flat albedo artwork texture sheet, fill entire frame, no light baked from one directional studio source. Design every pixel cluster as new art while following the original island placements exactly.

camouflage.prompt: Create a flat seamless square albedo texture of the camouflage cloth for the jacket worn by the existing Yugoslav Partisan game character. Use the reference image solely to match the jacket cloth’s woodland camouflage character: old olive and bottle green foliage, muted straw-tan light islands, and scattered deep red-brown / rust patches. Redraw the camouflage as believable retro realistic pixel art for a 3D character wearing it, big interconnected irregular stepped shapes composed of clearly square pixels, with some small leafy flecks inside the shapes. Main palette olive green, shaded forest green, dry beige, chestnut brown with reddish undertone. In a square patch there should be approximately four or five irregular chestnut patches, and several olive and tan shapes partially touching the square edges; sparse tan accents, not bright or white. No muddy dither, no single-pixel noise, no shadows, no clothing folds, no seams, no pockets, no collar, no buttons, no military insignia, no outlines around separate color areas, no photographic gradients, no background or border. This sole image is an edge-to-edge top-down textile print to be mapped across the jacket and two sleeves while retaining the existing game character’s independent plain brown trousers.

portrait.input: Earlier Pixel art face map, used as a UV layout reference
portrait.prompt: Edit the provided square pixel-art head and hands UV texture for a rigged 3D game character. Exact square flat albedo texture atlas filling the frame, no border, no rendering of a 3D view or graphic labels. Use the existing UV positions only. Replace the identity of the man completely with an unrelated adult Yugoslav partisan, around age 35, warm medium-tan skin, short nearly black hair with little to no volume and a visible high hairline, strong straight dark eyebrows, hazel olive-brown irises, large straight natural mustache only under the nose, clean shaved cheeks and jaw. He has a calm, steady expression and narrower closed lips. Draw the head at the top and the separate ears, keeping both eyes, nose nostrils, mouth seam, and inner ears at precisely the same UV centers as on the reference. Keep the square aspect and keep the face and head occupying the same top half. The isolated eyeball is specifically at bottom right, same UV pose, size, iris and pupil center, repainted hazel olive-brown to match. Preserve the locations of the non-head pieces across the bottom, including hands and mouth interiors; those pieces are only technical context. Redraw in chunky but natural realistic retro pixel art, sharply stepped edges, strong deliberate pixel clusters with a limited skin, black hair and warm brown shadow palette. No face from the reference, no blue eyes, no chestnut wavy hairstyle, no cosmetic lip shine, no beard on the chin, no extra accessories, no photographic noise, no centered portrait output. The output must remain a working unfolded UV atlas.

capBadgeStencil.method: Baked the bind-space star from core3d/actor/derived/ww2/sutjeskaLook.js onto the partisan.fbx cap UVs, with centre height 2.399 and radius 0.022. Sampled on a 3x subpixel grid at 768 × 768. Mask levels 192 and 255 select the red edge and fill.
